items.title: Ramsey Lewis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I said, “Have you talked to Rio Natsume in Japan?”

ctx.x: You got two historical peaks – at least two, if not many more, but definitely In Crowd and then Sun Goddess. It’s like, whew. And then that reference to “on the solo,” you put it out on your recent re-make. You still begin the tune with that.

I’m over in Japan last year, and we play the Blue Note there. We’ve been playing it for some time. He says, “Ramsey, I want you to come back next year.” I said, “Great.” He says, “But have you ever thought of putting your electric band back together?” I’ve been playing with a trio – there was a trio, and then there was this period in the ’70s, because of Sun Goddess, that I put the electric band together to be able to play Sun Goddess. I kept the electric band, and others – I needed voices too – I kept it…
said – the light came on – we’ll license the original and put that on the album, and that legitimizes the Sun Goddess tour. So that’s how it ended up on there.
